# Convert revenue from string to float, removing commas
# First, check for the presence of commas in revenue values
df['revenue_clean'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Verify the conversion worked by checking a few values
print("Sample of converted revenue:", df['revenue_clean'].head(5).values)

# Now filter for loyal, completed orders
loyal_completed = df[(df['customer_segment'] == 'loyal') & (df['status'] == 'completed')]

# Check for the six QA orders with 999999.99 revenue
qa_orders = loyal_completed[loyal_completed['revenue_clean'] == 999999.99]
print("Number of QA orders in loyal, completed set:", len(qa_orders))

# Remove QA orders
loyal_completed_clean = loyal_completed[loyal_completed['revenue_clean'] != 999999.99]

# Compute mean revenue
mean_revenue = loyal_completed_clean['revenue_clean'].mean()
print("Mean revenue (after removing QA orders):"," , mean_revenue)"}}
